messages.author: ef6cfc9d15fea2d1
messages.subject: 3D spatio-temproal modelling
parts:
Hello INLA helper,

Is that possible to do 3D spatio-temproal modelling with R-INLA, any examples (documents) for that?

Cheers,
Ke

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] 3D spatio-temproal modelling
parts:
Hi,

Yes, it's possible, but I'm not aware of any full examples.

For the 3D part, one option is to use the spde model constructions
from the experimental https://github.com/inlabru-org/inlamesh3d
package (provide a tetrahedralization of space, and it does the rest,
like inla.spde2.matern).
This can then be used as part of a separable space-time model, using
the "group" feature, e.g.
+ f(space, model=spde_3d, group = time, control.group=list(model="ar1"))
This is the method that requires the least new coding on your part.

Another alternative is to construct the spatial part as a rgeneric or
cgeneric model, and then proceed in the same way.

A third option is to implement the whole space-time model as an
rgeneric or cgeneric model.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] 3D spatio-temproal modelling
parts:
Without time, same approach, but with any available 2d model for xy, and z in the group model. With time, use z as as the 3rd coordinate of “space”. The interpretation of “space” isn’t restricted to physical space; it’s up to you.
Finn
